newsitem.title: UK: Emerging debt rallies on Greenspan comments.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt rallies on Greenspan comments.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices rallied on Friday following comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan in New York late Thursday, traders said.

"Greenspan's comments suggest it should not be regarded as an automatic increase (U.S. interest rates) one after the other, and that is giving some comfort to the market that the next rise is potentially being pushed back towards July rather than May," a head trader at a U.S. investment bank in London said.
Greenspan said he expected U.S. economic growth to slow later this year and into next but added the Fed would act if that did not prove to be the case.

While the emerging debt market rallied on his overnight comments, market experts said that each piece of U.S. economic data would be watched closely until the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting convenes on May 20.

"I would not say it is positive news but it certainly gives us a greater window before we would expect to see anything else and obviously we will evaluate the economic data as it comes through," the trader said.
Two key U.S. economic reports are the producer price index (PPI) due out Wednesday and the consumer price index (CPI) due out Thursday.

Although the credit fundamentals of many emerging market countries continue to improve, market experts said the Brady market has been taking its direction mainly from the U.S. Treasury market and the U.S. interest rate environment.
"U.S. interest rates are the main component of any price action," said another Brady trader from a U.S. investment bank.
Among Eastern European debt instruments, Poland continued to outperform the broader market on news earlier this week of a $1.69 billion buyback and hopes of a credit rating upgrade.
Poland's PDI bonds surged 1-1/8 to 84-1/8 bid and its par bonds firmed 7/8 to 56-3/8.
Earlier today, Standard and Poor's said that Poland's credit trend was fairly positive and that the U.S. rating agency would monitor the country's upcoming parliamentary elections closely.
Currenty, Poland's foreign currency debt is rated BBB minus by S&P and Baa3 by Moody's Investors Service Inc.
"I think Poland has a very strong bid and a very good story behind it. The fact that they are buying back and seeking an upgrade is building a great momentum for Poland," the second trader said.
Russia also posted sharp gains, with its Vneshconombank dollar loans rising 3/4 to 83-7/8 bid.
One emerging market trader attributed the price gains of Russian loans to client buying and an overall positive tone in the U.S. Treasury market.
In the Latin Brady market, prices also rose with fixed rate instruments generally outperforming the floating rate bonds.
Argentine pars were 1-1/4 better at 66-3/4 bid whereas the country's FRBs were 3/4 higher at 92-3/4 bid.
Venezuelan Pars were up one percentage point at 74 bid and Brazilian C' bonds were 1-3/8 stronger at 77-7/8 bid.
